approval.trigger: No review, wait, or gate before end users authorize or install. Review exists ONLY for the optional GitHub Marketplace listing (Request publish > an onboarding expert reaches out; paid listings need a verified-publisher org, 100 installations for GitHub Apps / 200 users for OAuth apps, and billing webhooks). blockers.detail: Installing a GitHub App on an org needs org-owner/repo-admin rights, and if the app requests org permissions the org owner must approve. With an active org application policy, OAuth app installs also need org-owner approval. Personal-account connections are frictionless.
blockers.howToClear: Target personal accounts first; document the org-owner approval step for enterprise users.
blockers.title: Org installs need org-owner approval

blockers.detail: The app name is capped at 34 characters and must be unique across all of GitHub.

flavor.why: GitHub's own docs open with 'Consider building a GitHub App instead of an OAuth app' and the decision guide says GitHub Apps are preferred in general. You get fine-grained permissions, a better consent screen (the installer picks exactly which repos), short-lived tokens, and far better rate limits. The user-delegation authorization flow is identical.

humanMust: Sign in (plus 2FA) and click through Settings > Developer settings
Choose visibility (public before other users can install) and permissions
Generate and safeguard the client secret / PEM private key
Click Request publish and accept the Marketplace agreement if listing
name: GitHub
nuances: Rate limits differ sharply: OAuth apps get 5,000 REST requests/hr/app (15,000 for Enterprise Cloud org-owned); GitHub App installation tokens scale with repos/users (5,000-15,000/hr). Token generation itself is capped at 2,000/hr/app.
Token lifetimes: OAuth app tokens are long-lived by default (opt-in to 8-hour access + refresh; refresh expires after 6 months of non-use). GitHub App installation tokens expire after 1 hour.
Device flow (headless/CLI) is supported by both types but must be explicitly enabled; the 8-character code is entered at github.com/login/device within 15 minutes.

Webhooks: GitHub Apps get one centralized webhook (disabled on uninstall); OAuth apps need per-repo webhooks that are not cleaned up on uninstall. Revoking all permissions from an OAuth app deletes app-generated SSH/deploy keys.
Marketplace listing is purely optional for users to connect; skip it unless you want discoverability.
prerequisites: A fallback app name (34-char cap, globally unique)
The fine-grained permissions your agent needs

steps.detail: Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps > New GitHub App. App name (max 34 chars, unique across GitHub), optional description, homepage URL. Set visibility: 'Only on this account' for private testing, 'Any account' (public) before other users can install; the public install URL is github.com/apps/APP-NAME/installations/new.

steps.detail: Select fine-grained permissions (e.g. read-only on contents) and set the webhook URL + secret if you need events. Least privilege keeps the consent screen clean.
steps.title: Choose permissions

steps.detail: On creation GitHub generates a PEM private key for minting installation tokens. Download it once and store it securely; it is also shown under the app's settings.
steps.title: Save the private key

steps.detail: Redirect users to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state (PKCE strongly recommended); exchange the code at POST github.com/login/oauth/access_token. User tokens from a GitHub App count against the user's own rate limit.
steps.title: Implement the user-delegation flow

steps.detail: (Optional, discoverability only) Draft the listing (description, logo, feature card, screenshots), set a pricing plan, handle billing webhooks, accept the Marketplace Developer Agreement, and click Request publish. No review timeline is stated.
